subject: Inspection gating, forensic access and MSA redline playbook
messages:
From: Daniel Crawford <daniel.crawford@mednova.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, security@mednova.com
Date: Wed, 04 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft security exhibit + asks on pen test / forensic access

Rachel — thanks for taking this. We finished an initial pass on the security exhibit and attached our redlines (MedNova_security_exhibit_redlines_20250603.docx). A few specific asks from procurement/security that we need clarified before legal will sign off: 

- Scope: We need the SOC 2 report plus a narrower set of inspection rights tied to a quarterly evidence cadence rather than open perpetual access. Can you confirm what assertions Redwood will share?
- Pen test language: MedNova requires a defined 30-day window notice and ephemeral staging access. We want to confirm whether Redwood can provide timeboxed SSH/API access and whether logs/forensic images can be exported if needed.
- Forensic access: If we discover potential data leakage we may request short-lived forensic snapshot exports; we need to understand Redwood's stance and any limitations.

We are on a compressed timeline — legal wants contract language before the end of next week. Can the Redwood team provide a single-page ops playbook (what access looks like, how evidence is delivered, how long request turnaround takes) plus proposed MSA redlines to close?

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Crawford
Senior Sourcing Manager, MedNova Health
security@mednova.com

Attachment: MedNova_security_exhibit_redlines_20250603.docx (docx, 52KB)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Crawford <daniel.crawford@mednova.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 05 Jun 2025 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft security exhibit + asks on pen test / forensic access

Hi Daniel — appreciate the clear list. Copying Laura (legal) and Ben (assurance) to capture the legal redlines and the operational constraints. Quick responses below and an ask: if you can call out the single highest-priority clause (e.g., full inspection vs. sampling-band access), we can tailor language faster.

Scope / SOC 2: Redwood can provide our most recent SOC 2 Type II report plus the mapping of relevant controls. We typically avoid broad perpetual inspection rights; our standard ask is to constrain inspection to scoped assertions (data isolation, encryption, incident logs). We can accept quarterly evidence windows with explicit sampling bands and a 48–72 hour evidence turnaround SLA for attestation artifacts.

Pen test window: We can commit to a 30-day notice for an agreed staging pen-test, with an ephemeral staging environment (timeboxed) and a mutually agreed test plan. We will require coordination with our infra on MFA/ephemeral creds and a short technical onboarding call.

Forensic exports: We can provide log exports and disk snapshots in most cases, but full forensic images are treated as exceptional and require an internal review plus an export approval workflow (2–3 business days). We will surface any legal/ops impacts up front.

Next steps I propose:
- Laura to provide MSA language we can put back into your draft.
- Ben to send a 1-page ops playbook and a short pen-test/checklist (who touches staging, how creds are issued, what we will not provide).
- I’ll schedule a 30-minute call with MedNova security and our infra leads to finalize a test window.

Attached: initial redline suggestions (I put informal comments in the doc).

—
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0123
Attachment: redwood_response_notes_20250605.txt (text, 6KB)

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Crawford <daniel.crawford@mednova.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Jun 2025 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft security exhibit + asks on pen test / forensic access

Daniel / Rachel — thanks. Attached is a tracked MSA redline that captures Redwood’s standard positions and the compromise language we can offer for an enterprise customer (MSA_redline_track_changes_20250605.pdf). High level: 

- Inspection rights: We are prepared to narrow inspection to scoped assertions and to formalize a quarterly evidence cadence. Contract language: we propose a clause that limits inspection to (a) SOC 2 reports and (b) timeboxed inspection windows for which Redwood will provide a defined evidence bundle. No perpetual wholesale access.
- Pen testing: Accept 30-day notice; pen-tests must follow an agreed test plan and only hit staging. We will provide ephemeral credentials and require proof of liability insurance / good-faith test rules.
- Forensic exports / incident response: We will provide log exports (raw logs, filtered) and application-level traces. For disk-level forensic images, we propose an escalation path: formal request + internal approval (48–72 hours) and a potential cost-recovery fee for engineering time if extensive.

Please review the attached PDF and call out any redlines you cannot accept. If MedNova agrees to the above guardrails, legal can accept the exhibit with the redlined MSA language. If you want, we can add a short appendix that enumerates the evidence bundle contents for each cadence (SOC attestations, access logs, KV cache traces, config manifests).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
Attachment: MSA_redline_track_changes_20250605.pdf (pdf, 48KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Crawford <daniel.crawford@mednova.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 06 Jun 2025 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft security exhibit + asks on pen test / forensic access

Daniel — quick technical note from the assurance side and the ops playbook (see pen-test-checklist_v1.xlsx). Keeping it short: 

- Staging access: We will spin up a staging slice with identical infra but anonymized sample data. Access is ephemeral (1–7 day window depending on scope). Credentials issued via our ephemeral creds service; all activity is logged to an immutable audit stream.
- Evidence bundle (quarterly window): SOC 2 + control matrix, S3 access logs (24–90 days retention), TLS termination configs, recent change-set manifests, and a sampling of request-level traces for agreed endpoints.
- Forensic images: engineering can produce disk snapshots but only after an incident triage; snapshots may include customer data and require export approvals + a written attestation. We can accept a clause allowing for forensics but the clause should require (a) a short escalation SLA (72 hours) and (b) cost-recovery for non-trivial engineering effort.

I’m happy to join the call Rachel will set up. If helpful I can circulate a one-page runbook that maps request -> owner -> SLA for each evidence type.

Ben Carter
Director, Assurance & Security Operations, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Attachment: pen-test-checklist_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 14KB)
